title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 语言文化 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）
meta: 主题语境：语言文化（人与社会·历史社会与文化·语言与文化）　|　核心词汇：phrase　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 phrase 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 the painter ① used the phrase that no visitor in the studio would have counted, and he said the using was the whole of the season. The ② phrase, meaning the expression itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; a phrase, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ phrase in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ phrase at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A phrase, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the painter said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the phrase was the whole of the matter, meaning the tone and not the expression. The ⑥ phrase, meaning the tone and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; phrase, he said, is either something you use or the only word that means both an expression and a tone. He said the tone is the part they remember.

By 1958 the ⑦ phrase had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ phrase of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of counting; phrase, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ phrase I remember is the expression counted in the catalogue, which closed in 1960 and is still counted as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ phrase, my mother said in 1962, is the only expression that improves by being counted; every phrase, she said, is a tone that has agreed to look like an expression. She said the tone was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 短语；说法（指画室里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 短语；说法（指那个短语本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：use the phrase 用这一个短语
D. n. 短语；说法（指留给孩子们留着的那一幅）
E. n. 短语之事（抽象总称，指一处画室的短语之事）
F. n. 短语；说法（指展品目录里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 短语、口吻（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 口吻（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: used the phrase that no visitor in the studio would have counted
The phrase, meaning the expression itself and not the brush
the phrase at the far easel
the phrase was the whole of the matter
the phrase had become a line in a catalogue
The phrase of the whole thing
A phrase, my mother said in 1962

answers.why: use the phrase 意为“用这一个短语”，1953 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯清点的一个短语做了一遍。
phrase 意为“短语；说法”，指那个短语本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被清点。
phrase 意为“短语；说法”，指画室里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
phrase 意为“短语；说法”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
phrase 意为“短语、口吻”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个口吻就是那件事的全部。
phrase 意为“口吻”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个短语，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
phrase 意为“短语；说法”，指展品目录里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1958 年这一个成了展品目录里的一行。
phrase 意为“短语之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的短语之事是一处画室和三个季度的清点。
phrase 意为“短语；说法”，我记得的是展品目录里清点过的那一个，1960 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一个。
phrase 为抽象总称，母亲 1962 年说，短语是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的短语。
